title: Streamline open-model onboarding with compatibility guardrails and pinning UX
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As part of the Model Catalog revamp we continue to onboard community/open-source models. Recent incidents and PR feedback have highlighted confusion around version variants, runtime compatibility (quantized vs fp16), and risk of breaking customers who pin to a specific variant. This ticket captures clarified requirements for the onboarding flow, acceptance criteria for UI/API guardrails, and the minimal migration strategy for already-onboarded models.

Problem statement: Onboarding engineers and model authors submit models with incomplete compatibility metadata and sometimes label a variant as 'v1' while runtime requirements differ. This causes runtime selection issues, failed rollouts, and increased support overhead. Product must provide clear fields, validations, and consumer-facing compatibility notes.

Goals:
- Define required metadata for any newly-registered open model (architecture, supported precisions, kv-cache shape assumptions, tokenizer id, expected max context length, compat matrix).
- Add a pinning UX and API semantics: how customers pin to major/minor/version+variant and what guarantees we provide.
- Implement validation rules in onboarding flow to catch obvious mismatches (e.g., tokenizer missing, declared max_ctx < model weights).
- Surface compatibility notes in catalog UI and model detail API.
- Provide a migration strategy and communication plan for existing catalog entries lacking required metadata.

Scope (in):
- PRD and acceptance criteria for frontend and API behavior.
- Automated onboarding validation checks integrated into model registration service.
- Compatibility notes schema and UI rendering.
- API semantics doc describing pin granularity and fallback rules.

Scope (out):
- Automated re-quantization or weight conversion.
- Model quality evaluation (LLM evals are tracked separately).

Constraints & decisions:
- Decision 2025-02-18: We will require tokenizer_id and max_context as mandatory strings at registration.
- Decision 2025-02-20: Pinning will support three granularities: major (model family), full-version (semantic version string), and variant-suffix (e.g., -q4_0, -fp16). We will provide backward-compatible fallback to best-effort variant if exact match not available, documented in the API.
- Trade-offs: Strict validation reduces support burden but increases friction for community submissions. We will ship helpful error messages and a simple CLI helper to generate metadata.

Acceptance Criteria: See acceptance_criteria field.

Rollout & migration notes:
- Phase 1 (feature flags): Expose validations as opt-in for internal teams and early adopters.
- Phase 2 (catalog enforcement): After 2 weeks, flip to required for new external submissions.
- Existing entries: We will open a backfill task to request metadata via email and create a temporary compatibility note "metadata missing - contact support" for entries not updated within 30 days.

Monitoring & success metrics:
- Reduction in onboarding-related support tickets by 60% within 90 days.
- 95% of new registrations pass validations without manual QA.
- Top 10 most-used models show correct compatibility notes in UI and API.

Documentation & artifacts: See links.
acceptance_criteria: API: New model registration endpoint returns 400 if tokenizer_id or max_context are missing; error messages include remediation steps
UI: Catalog model create/edit form includes explicit fields for supported_precisions and variant_suffix, with inline validation and examples
Pin semantics: Customer API docs define 'pin=major', 'pin=full', 'pin=variant' and show deterministic routing behavior for each; integration tests verify routing decisions
Compatibility matrix: Model detail API returns 'compatibility_notes' array and 'preferred_variant' string; catalog UI surfaces compatibility notes prominently
Validation checks: Automated onboarding validations detect mismatched declared max_context (declared < actual) and reject with clear guidance
Backfill: Existing 90% of previously onboarded open models either have completed metadata backfill or show a 'metadata pending' note within 30 days
End-to-end tests: CI includes at least 6 test cases across typical mismatch scenarios (missing tokenizer, incompatible precision, variant not found) and they pass
Docs: Confluence PRD and API docs updated with examples and CLI helper; internal changelog entry created
Security review: Security/compliance has signed off on any metadata fields that reference customer-owned keys or require additional export controls

notes_for_engineering: Validation logic should be pluggable and feature-flagged. Start with server-side checks in model-registration service and then mirror client-side form validation. Provide clear error codes for SDKs to map to UX flows. Include migration script to tag existing models with 'metadata_missing' for catalog visibility.
